title: Breaking News
goals: Tell what happened with the passive voice in the past simple (was / were + participle), with and without an agent.
Use by + agent and place adverbs (badly, completely, seriously) between was/were and the participle.
Extend the passive to other tenses: present, present continuous, present perfect, future and modals.
Talk about natural disasters, extreme weather and news with precise vocabulary.
Introduce news with Did you hear…? and mark ideas with The thing is… / The other thing is…
Write statistics about groups of people with correct subject-verb agreement.

learn.title: Passive voice in the past simple (was / were + participle)
learn.html:
In an active sentence the subject does the action (A student found a bag). In a passive sentence the subject receives the action (A bag was found on a bus). The passive is used when what happened matters more than who did it, or when we don't know or don't care who did it (very common in the news).

StructureExample
Affirmativesubject + was / were + participleThe airport was closed. Two cars were stolen.
Negativesubject + wasn't / weren't + participleThe passengers weren't injured.
QuestionWas / Were + subject + participle?Was the flight delayed? Were the roads closed?
Wh-Wh- + was / were + subject + participle?When was the bridge built?
  • Active → passive: the object becomes the subject: The police arrested two men. → Two men were arrested.
  • Only transitive verbs (with an object) have a passive. happen, arrive, die, occur are not used in the passive.
  • Irregular past participles are key: steal → stolen, break → broken, find → found, hit → hit, strike → struck.

watch.right: The bag was found on a bus.
watch.why: After was/were we use the participle (found), not the base form.

learn.title: by + agent and the position of adverbs
learn.html:
When the person who did the action (the agent) is important, it is added at the end with by: Three families were rescued by emergency workers. If the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant, it is left out: My car was stolen.

ActivePassive with by
An earthquake struck a town.A town was struck by an earthquake.
Careless campers caused the fires.The fires were caused by careless campers.
A tornado damaged a shopping mall.A shopping mall was damaged by a tornado.

Adverbs: in the past passive, adverbs usually go between was / were (not) and the participle: The mall was badly damaged. No one was seriously injured. The forest was completely destroyed. Power was temporarily disrupted. Homes were partially destroyed.

  • The agent with by goes at the end: damaged badly by a tornado sounds wrong; say badly damaged by a tornado.
  • After by use a noun or an object pronoun: by them, not by they.

watch.why: The adverb goes between was and the participle.

watch.wrong: A town was hit an earthquake.
watch.right: A town was hit by an earthquake.
watch.why: For the agent, by is missing.

watch.wrong: The fires were caused by they.
watch.right: The fires were caused by them.
watch.why: After by comes an object pronoun (them).
The degree adverb goes between was and the participle.

learn.title: The passive in other tenses
learn.html:
The passive is not only for the past simple. It is formed with be in the tense you need + participle.

TenseFormExample
Present simpleam / is / are + participleEnglish is spoken in many countries.
Present continuousis / are being + participleMany houses are still being repaired.
Present perfecthas / have been + participleThe suspect has been found.
Futurewill be + participleThe bridge will be rebuilt next year.
With modalscan / must / should be + participleDisasters can't be avoided, but their effects can be reduced.

In all cases the past participle goes at the end and be is the only thing that changes tense. The passive cannot be used with verbs without an object (happen, occur, arrive).

watch.right: The bridge will be rebuilt next year.

watch.right: The match has been canceled because of the rain.
Many houses are still being repaired.

Happen does not allow the passive.

learn.title: Writing statistics: subject-verb agreement
learn.html:
When writing percentages and fractions of a group of people, the verb agrees with the noun that follows of, not with the number.

NounVerbExample
Plural (students, people, us)plural80% of the students are interested in the news. The majority of students have Internet access.
Collective singular (class, population, group)singular80% of the class is interested in the news. About half of the class is interested in current events.
  • Four out of ten students read a newspaper (students is plural).
  • Approximately 20% of us get the news from TV (us is plural).
  • Useful expressions: the majority of, about half of, approximately, almost, only a quarter of, X out of ten.

learn.title: Introducing news: Did you hear…? and The thing is…
learn.html:
• Did you hear (about)…? / Have you heard (about)…? — to open a piece of news: Did you hear about all the trouble here last night?
  • Did I tell you? — Did I tell you? My car was broken into last Thursday night.
  • Guess what? / You know what? — to get attention before giving the news.
  • You know…? — to identify someone: You know that older guy on the first floor? His car was stolen.
  • The thing is, … — points out the key problem: The thing is, there aren't enough police on duty at night.
  • The other thing is, … — adds another problem.
  • The only thing is / was, … — presents a drawback: The only thing was, they damaged the ignition.
  • The best / funny / scary thing is, … — adds a nuance: The best thing was, the thieves didn't damage the car.

write.prompt: Write an informative news report of 180 to 250 words about a real or invented natural disaster (storm, earthquake, fire, flood) in a city. Use the passive voice in the past simple with at least three agents introduced by by, at least three adverbs (badly, completely, partially, seriously, temporarily) and a quote from a witness or an authority. Include a final detail about what will be done next, using the passive in the future (will be repaired).
targets: adverbs between was/were and the participle
checklist: Between 180 and 250 words
At least 6 sentences in the passive past simple
At least 3 sentences with by + agent
At least 3 adverbs placed between was/were and the participle
Correct irregular participles (stolen, broken, struck)
At least one sentence in the future passive (will be + participle)
No intransitive verbs in the passive (happen, occur)
write.model:
A powerful earthquake struck the city of Puerto Alegre early on Tuesday morning. The quake, which measured 6.8, was felt across the whole region at 5:12 a.m. Dozens of buildings were badly damaged, and the old market was completely destroyed by the shaking. Two bridges were seriously weakened by cracks, and one road was temporarily closed by the army.

More than 300 people were taken to shelters by volunteers, and food and blankets were delivered by the Red Cross. Many families were left without electricity because the main power line was partially broken. Several shops were robbed during the night, and some valuable items were stolen. A hospital in the north of the city was evacuated by doctors and nurses, and all the patients were safely moved to other clinics. Nobody was killed, but fifteen people were injured.

"We were sleeping when everything started shaking," said Marta López, a witness. "I have never been so scared." The mayor, Eduardo Rivas, said that the city had been lucky: "The response was quick, and I thank everyone who helped."

The damaged bridges will be repaired by engineers over the next month, and the market will be rebuilt with government funds. Schools will be inspected before classes begin again, and a new emergency plan will be presented to the public next week.

opinion with In my opinion / It seems to me that

Variety: the majority of, about half of, X out of ten

write.model:
Last month I carried out a small survey among 100 university students to find out how they keep up with the news. The results were interesting.

The majority of the students are interested in current events, but they do not read newspapers. About half of them get their information from social media, and 30 percent follow the headlines on news apps. Only 8 percent of the respondents watch television news every day. One out of ten students listens to podcasts, and two thirds of the group say that they check the news at least once a day. Seven out of ten people think that the press is not always honest, and a quarter of the students say they only read the headlines.

The class is divided on one point: a third of the students believe that online news is more reliable than television, while the rest disagree. The group is also young, so the figures show a clear trend. Most people read the news on their phones, and the number of readers who pay for a subscription is very low. Nobody in the survey reads a printed newspaper every day, which surprised me.

In my opinion, it is important to keep up with the news, because informed people make better decisions. It seems to me that we should check more than one source before we believe a story.

reading.title: After the Storm in San Rafael
reading.intro: Read the news article and answer.
paragraphs: On Tuesday night, a freak storm hit the town of San Rafael, a community of about 12,000 people in the mountains. According to the local weather service, the storm began at 9:40 p.m. with heavy rain, strong winds and, strangely, hailstones the size of golf balls. By midnight, a flash flood was rushing through the lower part of town.

Several streets were completely covered with water and dozens of cars were swept away. A small bridge near the market was badly damaged, and power was temporarily disrupted in most neighborhoods. Because of the weather, all flights from the regional airport were canceled, and schools were closed on Wednesday. Fortunately, no one was seriously injured. Thirty-two residents were rescued from their homes by firefighters and emergency workers, and most of them spent the night in the sports center.

Officials say that the main problem was not the rain itself, but the drainage system. "The pipes were built forty years ago," said the mayor, Elena Ruiz, "and they were never designed for storms like this." An investigation has been opened, and a report is expected next month. In the meantime, the bridge will be repaired, and the damaged roofs will be fixed with money from the state emergency fund.

The real story, however, was not the damage but the response. By Wednesday morning, more than two hundred volunteers had arrived at the sports center. Students carried water bottles, bakers donated bread, and a local radio station was turned into an emergency information line. "I didn't know most of my neighbors," said Carlos Medina, a retired teacher whose garage was flooded. "Now I know all of their names."

A recent survey of the town shows how important local news was during the emergency. Almost 70 percent of residents say they received their first alert from the radio or from neighbors, and only about a quarter of them got it from the website of a national newspaper. The majority of people are still waiting for permanent repairs, but about half of the town is already planning a community meeting to discuss a better warning system.

Local businesses also helped. The owner of a hardware store, Rosa Beltrán, gave away tools and plastic sheets to families whose roofs were damaged. "Nobody was asked to pay," she said. "We were all affected by the same storm." Several hotels in nearby towns offered free rooms to residents whose homes were badly flooded, and a regional newspaper started a fund that has already collected about $8,000.
"The thing is," Mayor Ruiz added, "disasters can't be avoided, but their effects can be reduced. Preparation is what makes the difference."

listening.title: Trouble on our street
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two neighbors. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Did you hear about all the trouble on our street last night?
Guess what? Mr. Torres's car was stolen from the parking lot.
No, nobody was injured, but the police came too late. The thing is, there weren't enough officers on duty at night.
That's true. And the other thing is, the car alarm was never repaired. Did I tell you? My car was broken into last month.
Just a bag and some tools. The only thing was, the ignition was damaged when they tried to start it.
That's awful. Was the car found?
Yes, it was found two days later by a neighbor. The best thing is, the thieves didn't take the engine!
Ha! Well, I'm glad it was recovered. Is there anything in the news about it?
Yes. A short report was published this morning in the local newspaper. I saw it online.
